Hi Erin — thanks for the note and great to hear the team found the demo useful. I’m attaching our current subprocessor CSV and a quick annotated dataflow. High level answers below:

- Attached: redwood-subprocessors-20250730.csv (columns: vendor, role, country, SCCs/Standard Contracting note, provisional?)
- Transient partners: our edge CDN (EdgeLine) may cache telemetry for up to 72 hours in regional POPs; default routing for the US pilot keeps compute and storage in the US but CDN POPs occasionally route through nearby regions for optimization.
- Encryption: all customer content is encrypted at rest. For hosted customers we manage keys by default; we offer KMS/HSM integration on Dedicated and Private plans (customer-managed keys).

A couple of clarifying questions so we can mark items as final vs provisional:
1) Is NorthWind’s pilot strictly limited to US-only processing for regulatory reasons, or would temporary POP routing be acceptable if data residency stays in US storage?
2) Do you need SOC 2 supporting artifacts or just the roster and diagram for procurement this round?

I’ve looped in Kimberly (privacy/legal) for any contract-level notes and Jordan for procurement/ops follow-up.

Thanks,
